items.title: MSME Festive Invoice Discounting Jumped 33% in 2026
items.dek: Small sellers turned unpaid festive invoices into cash far more often this year, up 33% on 2025. Here is the arithmetic for a shop that waits to be paid.

cta.text: Waiting 90 days to be paid is a choice you can price. Work out how much cash a late-paying buyer locks up before you quote the order.
cta.label: Open the Working Capital Calculator

body_en:
Small businesses that sell to bigger buyers on credit financed more than ₹20,000 crore of festive stock this year by discounting unpaid invoices, according to the Festive Insights Report from M1xchange, an RBI-licensed invoice discounting platform. That is 33% more than the ₹15,000 crore financed in the 2025 festive season. As of October 28, 2026, the platform had already crossed its entire previous-year festive volume with a couple of days of peak activity still to come.

For a shop, a distributor or a small manufacturer, the story is not the headline number. It is the reason the number grew: more small suppliers stopped waiting 60 or 90 days to be paid and turned the invoice into cash instead.

What the festive numbers show

The report, from M1xchange, tracks invoice discounting across the festive period, when shops and factories stock up months before they are paid. Pre-festive financing volumes crossed ₹20,000 crore in 2026, up from ₹15,000 crore in 2025. That is a rise of ₹5,000 crore, or one rupee in three more than last year. Average daily festive financing jumped more than 40% year on year, and M1xchange expects the full season to grow by about 30% over 2025.

The sector split tells you where the stocking pressure sits. Invoicing during the festive period rose 28% over the pre-festive months in consumer durables, 27% in chemicals, 20% in fast-moving consumer goods and 19% in metals and mining. E-retail and e-commerce invoicing grew more than 100%, and paints saw a sharp jump, though from a smaller base.

Why a shop runs short of cash in the festive season

Festive demand is good news and a cash trap at the same time. A supplier has to buy raw material, pay wages and pay for transport in September and October, but the big buyer pays only after the goods are sold and the invoice clears its approval cycle. The gap between paying out and being paid in is where a small business runs out of money.

Traditionally that gap was filled by a working capital loan from a bank, or by borrowing from a moneylender at a rate nobody writes down. Invoice discounting is the third route: the supplier uploads an accepted invoice to a platform, banks and non-bank lenders bid to buy it at a discount, and the supplier gets most of the money now instead of all of it later.

The arithmetic on a ₹10 lakh invoice

Take a supplier who delivers ₹10,00,000 of goods to a large buyer on 90-day terms. If the supplier waits the full 90 days, it gets ₹10,00,000 at the end and nothing before that.

Now discount the invoice. Suppose the winning bid works out to 12% a year. For 90 days, that is a quarter of a year, so the discount is 3% of ₹10,00,000, or ₹30,000. The supplier receives ₹9,70,000 within days and the platform collects the full ₹10,00,000 from the buyer on the due date.

The trade is simple to read: ₹30,000 buys three months of cash. If that ₹9,70,000 lets the supplier take a second order, or avoid a 24% moneylender, the discount is cheap. If the supplier already sits on cheap bank credit and does not need the money early, it is not. Financing on the platform is collateral-free and the lender has no claim on the seller if the buyer fails to pay, so the risk the seller takes on is the discount, not the debt.

The micro segment is the real story

The fastest growth came from the smallest businesses. Financing for the micro segment more than doubled, to about ₹3,000 crore, and micro enterprises are now the quickest-growing group using formal invoice discounting. Sundeep Mohindru, founder of M1xchange, called the doubling a sign that formal credit is spreading to businesses that used to rely on informal borrowing.

That matters because a micro supplier is exactly the business with no cushion. A ₹10,00,000 order can be a third of its yearly turnover, and a late payment can stall the next order. When a platform advances the cash against an accepted invoice, the business stops being a bank for its own customer.

What TReDS changes for a small supplier

M1xchange runs on TReDS, the Trade Receivables Discounting System that the Reserve Bank of India regulates. Buyers — large companies, government departments and public sector units — accept an invoice on the platform, and lenders then bid to discount it. The government has also pushed public sector buyers to settle MSME invoices through these platforms, which widens the set of invoices a small supplier can put up.

The practical point for a supplier is eligibility. Your invoice has to be accepted by the buyer and raised on a buyer who is on the platform. If your biggest customer is a large company or a public sector unit, the invoice is likely eligible; if your customer is another small shop, it usually is not.

What it means for your business

If you supply a big buyer on credit, this is worth one afternoon of work. Check whether that buyer is on a TReDS platform and whether your invoices are being accepted there. Compare the discount rate a platform quotes with the interest you pay on your overdraft or working capital loan: if the discount costs less, the platform is the cheaper money. If your buyer pays on time and your bank credit is already cheap, the discount is a cost you can skip.

The wider signal is that formal credit for small suppliers is getting easier and more competitive, and the festive numbers show small businesses are using it. The lesson is not to borrow more. It is to stop funding a large customer's working capital for free, and to price that delay into every quote you give.
body_hinglish:
Chhote businesses jo bade buyers ko credit par maal bechte hain, unhone is saal ₹20,000 crore se zyada ka festive stock finance kiya — unpaid invoices ko discount karke. Ye M1xchange ki Festive Insights Report ke hisaab se hai, jo RBI-licensed invoice discounting platform hai. Ye 2025 ke ₹15,000 crore se 33% zyada hai. 28 October 2026 tak platform apne pichle saal ke pura festive volume se aage nikal chuka tha, aur peak activity ke do din abhi baaki the.

Dukaan, distributor ya chhote manufacturer ke liye asli baat headline number nahi hai. Asli baat ye hai ki number kyun badha: zyada chhote suppliers ne 60 ya 90 din payment ka intezaar chhod kar invoice ko cash mein badal diya.

Festive numbers kya dikhate hain

M1xchange ki report festive period mein invoice discounting track karti hai — wo waqt jab dukaanein aur factories mahino pehle stock bhar leti hain, par payment baad mein milti hai. Pre-festive financing 2026 mein ₹20,000 crore se upar gayi, jo 2025 mein ₹15,000 crore thi. Ye ₹5,000 crore ka badlav hai, yaani har teen rupaye par ek rupaya zyada. Average daily festive financing pichle saal se 40% se zyada badhi, aur M1xchange ko pura season 2025 se lagbhag 30% badhne ki ummeed hai.

Sector ka bantwara batata hai stock ka dabaav kahan hai. Festive period mein invoicing pre-festive mahino se consumer durables mein 28%, chemicals mein 27%, FMCG mein 20% aur metals & mining mein 19% badhi. E-retail aur e-commerce invoicing 100% se zyada badhi, aur paints mein tez uchhal aayi, chahe base chhota tha.

Festive season mein dukaan ke paas cash kyun kam padta hai

Festive demand ek saath achhi khabar aur cash ka jaal dono hai. Supplier ko September-October mein raw material kharidna, wages dena aur transport bharna padta hai, par bada buyer goods bikne aur invoice approval ke baad hi pay karta hai. Paisa dene aur paisa milne ke beech ka gap wahi hai jahan chhota business phans jata hai.

Pehle ye gap bank ke working capital loan se, ya aise moneylender se bharta tha jiska rate koi likhta nahi. Invoice discounting teesra raasta hai: supplier accepted invoice platform par daalta hai, banks aur non-bank lenders usse discount par kharidne ki bid lagate hain, aur supplier ko baad ke poore paise ki jagah abhi zyada hissa mil jata hai.

₹10 lakh invoice ka hisaab

Maan lijiye ek supplier bade buyer ko 90 din ke terms par ₹10,00,000 ka maal deta hai. Agar supplier poore 90 din wait kare, to use aakhir mein ₹10,00,000 milta hai, usse pehle kuch nahi.

Ab invoice discount kar dijiye. Maan lijiye winning bid 12% saalana banti hai. 90 din yaani saal ka chauthai, to discount ₹10,00,000 ka 3%, yaani ₹30,000. Supplier ko kuch dinon mein ₹9,70,000 mil jate hain aur platform due date par buyer se pura ₹10,00,000 wasool karta hai.

Deal padhna aasan hai: ₹30,000 teen mahine ka cash kharidta hai. Agar us ₹9,70,000 se supplier doosra order le leta hai, ya 24% wale moneylender se bach jata hai, to discount sasta hai. Agar supplier ke paas pehle se sasta bank credit hai aur paisa jaldi ki zarurat nahi, to ye fayda nahi. Platform par financing collateral-free hai aur buyer na dene par lender ka seller par koi claim nahi hota, to seller ka risk discount hai, karza nahi.

Asli kahani micro segment ki hai

Sabse tez growth sabse chhote businesses se aayi. Micro segment ki financing double se zyada badh kar lagbhag ₹3,000 crore ho gayi, aur micro enterprises ab formal invoice discounting use karne wala sabse tez badhta group hain. M1xchange ke founder Sundeep Mohindru ne is doubling ko is baat ka saboot kaha ki formal credit un businesses tak pahunch raha hai jo pehle informal udhaar par the.

Ye isliye maayne rakhta hai kyunki micro supplier ke paas koi cushion nahi hota. ₹10,00,000 ka order uski saalana turnover ka teesra hissa ho sakta hai, aur ek late payment agla order rok sakti hai. Jab platform accepted invoice par cash de deta hai, to business apne hi customer ka bank banna band kar deta hai.

TReDS chhote supplier ke liye kya badalta hai

M1xchange TReDS par chalta hai — Trade Receivables Discounting System, jise Reserve Bank of India regulate karta hai. Buyers, yaani badi companies, government departments aur public sector units, platform par invoice accept karte hain, aur phir lenders usse discount karne ki bid lagate hain. Sarkar ne public sector buyers ko bhi MSME invoices in platforms se settle karne ke liye kaha hai, jisse chhote supplier ke liye eligible invoices badh jate hain.

Supplier ke liye asli baat eligibility hai. Invoice buyer dwara accept hona chahiye aur aise buyer par bana ho jo platform par ho. Agar aapka sabse bada customer badi company ya public sector unit hai, to invoice aksar eligible hota hai; agar customer doosri chhoti dukaan hai, to aksar nahi.

Aapke business ke liye iska matlab

Agar aap bade buyer ko credit par supply karte hain, to ye ek dopahar ke kaam ki baat hai. Dekhiye ki wo buyer kisi TReDS platform par hai ya nahi, aur aapke invoices wahan accept ho rahe hain ya nahi. Platform ka discount rate apne overdraft ya working capital loan ke byaaj se milaiye: agar discount sasta hai, to platform sasta paisa hai. Agar buyer time par pay karta hai aur aapka bank credit pehle se sasta hai, to discount ek kharach hai jise chhod sakte hain.

Badi baat ye hai ki chhote suppliers ke liye formal credit aasan aur competitive hota ja raha hai, aur festive numbers dikhate hain ki chhote businesses ise use kar rahe hain. Seekh ye nahi ki zyada udhaar lena hai. Seekh ye hai ki bade customer ka working capital muft mein fund karna band kijiye, aur har quote mein us delay ka daam jodiye.

items.title: GST From Nov 1: Easier Discounts, Faster Refunds
items.dek: From November 1, a post-sale discount needs only a credit note, inverted-duty refunds release 90% early, and the ₹1,000 export refund floor is scrapped.

cta.text: A post-sale discount now cuts your taxable value with a credit note alone. Work out the GST on the discounted price before you quote it.
cta.label: Open the GST Calculator

body_en:
Three changes to India's GST law take effect on November 1, 2026. They come from Notification No. 03/2026–Central Tax dated October 26, 2026, which brought sections 153, 154 and 155 of the Finance Act, 2026 into force and amended sections 15, 34 and 54 of the CGST Act, 2017. The measures were first announced in the 2026-27 budget.

For a shop, a distributor or a small exporter, they matter for one reason: they move the work from the front of a sale to the back. Paperwork after the invoice now decides how much tax you actually pay.

What changes on November 1

  • Post-sale discounts: the old conditions — a discount agreed in advance and tied to specific invoices — are dropped. A credit note from the supplier and a reversal of input tax credit by the buyer are now the test.
  • Credit notes: section 34 now expressly covers a discount given under the new valuation rule.
  • Refunds: a 90% provisional refund is extended to businesses whose input tax is higher than their output tax.
  • Export refunds: the ₹1,000 minimum that blocked tiny refunds no longer applies to tax paid on goods exported out of India.

The credit note is now the whole game

Under the old section 15(3)(b), a discount given after the supply could reduce the taxable value only if it was agreed before the sale, linked to particular invoices, and the buyer reversed the credit. Those first two conditions are gone. What remains is that the supplier must issue a credit note and the buyer must reverse the input tax credit attributable to the discount.

That is a real relief for year-end and volume schemes. A manufacturer who promises dealers an incentive in April, but only knows the payout in March, no longer has to defend the arrangement as if the exact figure were fixed up front.

The arithmetic on a ₹10 lakh discount

Say a dealer earns a ₹10 lakh discount for the year, expressed before tax. At 18% GST, the tax on that discount is ₹1,80,000, so the supplier issues a credit note for ₹11,80,000.

The supplier then reduces taxable value and output tax by ₹1,80,000, provided the credit note is issued in time. The dealer reverses ₹1,80,000 of input tax credit. If the dealer had already claimed that credit, the reversal keeps the government's books whole; if the dealer does not reverse it, the supplier loses the benefit.

Before November 1 the same discount could be questioned because it was not fixed before the sale. Now the test is simpler: was a credit note issued, and did the buyer reverse the credit?

Faster refunds when your input tax is higher

When the tax on your inputs is higher than the tax on what you sell, credit piles up month after month. Section 54(6) already allowed a 90% provisional refund for zero-rated supplies. The amendment extends that facility to inverted duty structure refunds, so the law itself now backs a faster release.

Take a business with ₹1 crore of credit stuck every year. Under the new rule, ₹90 lakh of it can come back early once conditions are met and the claim is verified. The remaining ₹10 lakh follows after verification. For a firm that borrows to fund working capital, getting ₹90 lakh early can cut the interest it pays.

Early is not final. A refund later found to be too high can be recovered, so reconcile your returns before you file, not after a notice arrives.

Small exporters: the ₹1,000 floor goes

Section 54(14) said no refund under ₹1,000 would be paid. From November 1 that limit does not apply to the refund of tax on goods exported out of India with payment of tax. A small exporter shipping low-value consignments will no longer see a refund held back just because it fell under the threshold.

The exception is narrow. It covers goods exported with payment of tax, not refunds on the export of services, and not other refund categories. Do not stretch it.

What it means for your shop

Write your discount schemes down, even though advance agreement is no longer a legal condition, and set a calendar for credit notes. Check that any buyer who takes a discount reverses the matching input tax credit, or the tax saving disappears. If you carry a large pile of input credit because of the inverted duty structure, plan the refund claim and reconcile first. If you export goods, list the small refunds that were blocked earlier and claim them from November 1.

None of this removes paperwork. It moves the burden to the back of the sale: credit notes, reversals and reconciliations now carry the weight.
body_hinglish:
1 November 2026 se GST kanoon mein teen badlav lagu honge. Ye Notification No. 03/2026–Central Tax, 26 October 2026 se aaye hain, jisne Finance Act 2026 ki sections 153, 154 aur 155 ko lagu kiya aur CGST Act 2017 ki sections 15, 34 aur 54 ko badla. Ye kadam 2026-27 budget mein announce hue the.

Dukaan, distributor ya chhote exporter ke liye baat ek hai: kaam sale ke aage se hat kar peeche aa gaya hai. Ab invoice ke baad ka paperwork tay karta hai ki aap kitna tax bharenge.

1 November se kya badlega

  • Post-sale discount: purani shartein — discount pehle se tay ho aur khaas invoices se juda ho — hata di gayi hain. Ab supplier ka credit note aur buyer dwara input tax credit ka reversal hi kasauti hai.
  • Credit note: section 34 ab naye valuation rule ke discount ko saaf-saaf cover karta hai.
  • Refund: 90% provisional refund un businesses ko bhi milega jinka input tax output tax se zyada hai.
  • Export refund: ₹1,000 ki minimum hadd, jo chhote refund rok deti thi, ab India se bahar bheje gaye goods par bhare tax par lagu nahi hogi.

Ab credit note hi asli khel hai

Purane section 15(3)(b) mein supply ke baad ka discount taxable value kam kar sakta tha sirf tab, jab wo sale se pehle tay ho, khaas invoices se juda ho, aur buyer credit reverse kare. Pehli do shartein khatam. Ab sirf itna chahiye: supplier credit note de aur buyer discount ka input tax credit reverse kare.

Ye saal ke ant aur volume schemes ke liye asli rahat hai. Manufacturer April mein dealers ko incentive ka wada karta hai, par pura hisaab March mein banta hai — ab use ye sabit karne ki zarurat nahi ki figure pehle se fix tha.

₹10 lakh discount ka hisaab

Maan lijiye ek dealer ko saal ka ₹10 lakh discount milta hai, tax se pehle. 18% GST par us discount ka tax ₹1,80,000 banta hai, to supplier ₹11,80,000 ka credit note deta hai.

Supplier taxable value aur output tax ₹1,80,000 se kam kar deta hai, bas credit note time par milna chahiye. Dealer ₹1,80,000 ka input tax credit reverse karta hai. Agar dealer ne wo credit pehle le liya tha, to reversal sarkar ka hisaab barabar rakhta hai; agar dealer reverse nahi karta, to supplier ko fayda nahi milega.

1 November se pehle yahi discount sawal mein aa sakta tha kyunki wo sale se pehle tay nahi tha. Ab test aasan hai: credit note aaya, aur buyer ne credit reverse kiya ya nahi?

Jab input tax output se zyada ho to refund jaldi

Jab input par tax output se zyada ho, to credit har mahine jama hota rehta hai. Section 54(6) pehle se zero-rated supply ke liye 90% provisional refund deta tha. Amendment ab inverted duty structure refund par bhi ye suvidha deta hai, to kanoon khud tez release ko support karta hai.

Maan lijiye ek business ka ₹1 crore credit har saal atka rehta hai. Naye rule se ₹90 lakh jaldi wapas aa sakta hai, jab shartein poori ho aur claim verify ho jaye. Baaki ₹10 lakh verification ke baad milta hai. Jo firm working capital ke liye udhaar leti hai, uske liye ₹90 lakh jaldi milna byaaj bacha sakta hai.

Jaldi ka matlab final nahi. Baad mein zyada nikla refund recover ho sakta hai, isliye return notice se pehle, filing se pehle mila lijiye.

Chhote exporters: ₹1,000 ki hadd khatam

Section 54(14) kehta tha ki ₹1,000 se kam refund nahi milega. 1 November se ye hadd India se bahar bheje gaye goods par bhare tax ke refund par lagu nahi hogi. Kam value ke consignment bhejne wale chhote exporter ka refund ab sirf is wajah se nahi rukega ki wo threshold se neeche tha.

Chhoot sankri hai. Ye sirf un goods par hai jo tax bharkar export hue, services ke export par nahi, aur baaki refund categories par nahi. Isko badha-chadha kar mat samjhiye.

Aapki dukaan ke liye iska matlab

Apni discount schemes likh kar rakhiye, chahe pehle se tay karna ab kanooni shart na ho, aur credit note ke liye calendar banaiye. Dekhiye ki discount lene wala buyer matching input tax credit reverse kare, warna tax ki bachat gayab ho jayegi. Agar inverted duty structure ki wajah se aapka input credit bahut jama hai, to refund claim plan kijiye aur pehle mila lijiye. Agar aap goods export karte hain, to pehle ruke chhote refunds ki list bana kar 1 November se claim kijiye.

Isse paperwork khatam nahi hota. Bojh sale ke peeche chala jata hai: credit notes, reversals aur reconciliations hi ab asli kaam hain.

items.title: RELIEF Scheme Extended to March 2027: What MSMEs Get
items.dek: India extended the RELIEF export scheme to March 31, 2027, keeping 95% ECGC risk cover for West Asia shipments. Here is exactly what an MSME exporter gets.

cta.text: Extra freight and war-risk premiums are paid up front and any reimbursement comes months later. See how much working capital that ties up before you accept the order.
cta.label: Open the Working Capital Calculator

body_en: The Commerce Ministry extended the RELIEF scheme for exporters on Monday, October 26, 2026, pushing its run to March 31, 2027. RELIEF stands for Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation, and it sits under the Export Promotion Mission. The reason it exists is simple: shipping through the Gulf and West Asia has become both costly and unpredictable, and the exporter is who pays for that.
What the extension actually keeps

Only one part of the scheme has been carried forward, and it is Component II. That component gives exporters 95% risk cover through the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) on upcoming shipments to a listed set of countries, and it now runs to the end of the financial year. The original scheme was notified in March 2026 with an outlay of ₹497 crore and covered consignments to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Iraq, Iran, Israel and Yemen.
What 95% cover means in rupees

Risk cover is not a subsidy, it is an insurance backstop, so the number it produces is what you get back when a buyer does not pay. Suppose you ship ₹20,00,000 of goods to Dubai and the buyer defaults. At 95% cover, ECGC pays ₹19,00,000 and you absorb the remaining 5%, which is ₹1,00,000. If your margin on that order is 10%, you had ₹2,00,000 of gross profit and you are left with ₹1,00,000. The cover stops the order from becoming a total loss; it does not make you whole.

That is still worth having. Without the cover the same default costs you the full ₹20,00,000, and that is the kind of hit that closes a small firm. This is the part of the scheme that MSME exporters say is genuinely working, and it is why the extension was welcomed even by groups that are unhappy about the rest of it.
What MSME exporters lost

The complaint is about Component III, which was left out of the extension. That component reimbursed up to 50% of the extra freight and insurance costs for MSME exporters who are not covered by ECGC, with a ceiling of ₹50 lakh per exporter and ₹282 crore set aside for it. Exporters without credit insurance therefore get nothing from this extension, even though the war-risk surcharge and the freight hikes are exactly the costs they are carrying.

Vinod Kumar, president of the India SME Forum, said the exclusion leaves “thousands of micro and small enterprises operating without credit insurance ... to absorb crushing freight hikes and war-risk surcharges alone”. Animesh Saxena, a former president of FISME, said MSMEs cannot negotiate rates the way large corporates can and asked for a freight subsidy at the national level; Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh already run their own. Exporters have also asked for a 24-month rolling scheme, arguing that a six-to-nine-month production and shipping cycle makes a March deadline hard to plan around.
Why the freight bill is the real problem

Run the arithmetic on a year of exports and the gap becomes clear. Say a small firm ships ₹1 crore of goods to West Asia in a year. If the war-risk premium and higher freight add 6% on top of what the same cargo cost before, that is ₹6,00,000 of extra cost in the year. Under Component III half of it, ₹3,00,000, would have come back, and the full ₹6,00,000 sits well under the ₹50 lakh cap. With Component III gone, the firm absorbs all ₹6,00,000.

On a business whose net margin is 8%, ₹6,00,000 is the profit on ₹75,00,000 of sales. In other words, the freight increase alone can wipe out the margin on three-quarters of the year's turnover, which is why the ask is for a subsidy and not just for insurance.
What it means for your business

If you export to West Asia and you already hold ECGC cover, the extension is straightforward good news: your shipments are protected at 95% until March 2027 and there is nothing extra to do to claim it. If you are an MSME without credit insurance, plan on paying the full freight and war-risk cost yourself, because this extension does not reimburse any of it.

Either way the practical step is the same. Put the extra freight and premium into your cost sheet as a line item, not a footnote, and check what it does to your break-even before you quote the next order. Extra freight and war-risk premiums are paid up front while any reimbursement arrives months later, so the cash has to come from somewhere in between. Working out how much working capital that ties up, and how much of the extra cost your price can carry, is the difference between an order that looks busy and an order that pays.
body_hinglish: Commerce Ministry ne Monday, October 26, 2026 ko exporters ke liye RELIEF scheme ko March 31, 2027 tak badha diya. RELIEF ka matlab hai Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation, aur ye Export Promotion Mission ke andar chalti hai. Iski zaroorat isliye hai kyunki Gulf aur West Asia ke raste se shipping mehngi bhi ho gayi hai aur bharosemand bhi nahi rahi, aur iska bill exporter bharta hai.
Extension mein kya bacha

Scheme ka sirf ek hissa aage badhaya gaya hai, aur wo hai Component II. Ye component exporters ko listed deshon ki upcoming shipments par Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) ke through 95% risk cover deta hai, aur ab ye financial year ke end tak chalega. Original scheme March 2026 mein ₹497 crore ke outlay ke saath notify hui thi aur isme UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Iraq, Iran, Israel aur Yemen ki consignments cover hoti thi.
95% cover ka matlab rupaye mein

Risk cover koi subsidy nahi hai, ye insurance ka sahara hai, to iska number wahi hai jo buyer na dene par wapas milta hai. Maan lo tum ₹20,00,000 ka maal Dubai bhejte ho aur buyer default kar deta hai. 95% cover par ECGC ₹19,00,000 deta hai aur bache 5% yaani ₹1,00,000 tum par aate hain. Agar us order par tumhara margin 10% hai, to tumhare paas ₹2,00,000 ka gross profit tha aur ab ₹1,00,000 bacha. Cover order ko poore nuksan banne se bachata hai; ye tumhe pura nahi karta.

Phir bhi ye kaafi hai. Cover ke bina wahi default tumhe poore ₹20,00,000 ka nuksan deta hai, aur itna jhatka chhoti firm ko band kar deta hai. Yahi hissa hai jise MSME exporters sach mein kaam karta hua maante hain, isliye baaki baaton se na khush hone wale groups ne bhi extension ko welcome kiya.
MSME exporters ne kya khoya

Shikayat Component III ki hai, jise extension mein shamil nahi kiya gaya. Wo component un MSME exporters ko, jo ECGC ke cover mein nahi aate, unke extra freight aur insurance cost ka 50% tak reimburse karta tha, ₹50 lakh per exporter ki limit ke saath, aur uske liye ₹282 crore rakhe gaye the. Credit insurance ke bina wale exporters ko is extension se kuch nahi milta, jabki war-risk surcharge aur freight hike wahi costs hain jo wo utha rahe hain.

India SME Forum ke president Vinod Kumar ne kaha ki is chhoot se “thousands of micro and small enterprises operating without credit insurance ... to absorb crushing freight hikes and war-risk surcharges alone”. FISME ke former president Animesh Saxena ne kaha ki MSMEs badi companies ki tarah rates negotiate nahi kar sakte, aur unhone national level par freight subsidy maangi; Haryana, Uttar Pradesh aur Madhya Pradesh apni subsidy chala rahe hain. Exporters ne 24 mahine ki rolling scheme bhi maangi hai, ye kehte hue ki chhe se nau mahine ke production aur shipping cycle ke saath March ki deadline plan karna mushkil hai.
Asli problem freight bill hai

Ek saal ke exports ka hisaab lagao to gap saaf dikhta hai. Maan lo ek chhoti firm saal mein ₹1 crore ka maal West Asia bhejti hai. Agar war-risk premium aur mehnga freight pehle ke muqable 6% jod de, to saal ka extra cost ₹6,00,000 banega. Component III ke under iska aadha, ₹3,00,000, wapas mil jaata, aur poora ₹6,00,000 ₹50 lakh ki limit se kaafi kam hai. Component III hatne ke baad firm poora ₹6,00,000 khud jhelti hai.

Jis business ka net margin 8% hai, uske liye ₹6,00,000 matlab ₹75,00,000 ki sales ka profit. Yaani sirf freight ka badhaawa saal ke teen-chauthai turnover ka margin kha sakta hai, isliye maang insurance ke saath subsidy ki bhi hai.
Tumhare business ke liye iska matlab

Agar tum West Asia ko export karte ho aur tumhare paas ECGC cover hai, to extension seedhi achhi khabar hai: March 2027 tak tumhari shipments 95% par protected hain aur claim ke liye kuch alag karna nahi hai. Agar tum ECGC cover ke bina wale MSME ho, to poora freight aur war-risk cost khud dene ki tayari rakho, kyunki is extension mein uska ek paisa bhi reimburse nahi hota.

Dono haal mein practical step ek hi hai. Extra freight aur premium ko apni cost sheet mein ek line item ki tarah daalo, footnote ki tarah nahi, aur agla order quote karne se pehle dekho ki tumhara break-even kahan jaata hai. Extra freight aur war-risk premium pehle dena padta hai aur reimbursement mahino baad aata hai, to beech ke samay ka cash kahin se aana padega. Ye pata karna ki isse kitna working capital block hota hai, aur tumhari price is extra cost ka kitna hissa utha sakti hai, ek busy dikhne wale order aur paisa dene wale order ka farak hai.

items.title: Rupee Falls to 95.22: What It Costs Importers
items.dek: A third straight day of losses left the rupee at 95.22 against the dollar on October 26. Here is what that adds to an import bill and pays an exporter.

cta.text: The exchange rate is one line in what a landed unit costs you. Put it beside freight, duty and insurance and see the true cost before you quote a price.
cta.label: Open the Landed Cost Calculator

body_en: The rupee fell for the third straight day on Monday, October 26, 2026, settling 29 paise lower at 95.22 against the U.S. dollar. It opened the day at 94.92, touched an intra-day low of 95.26 and closed at 95.22. The fall came on top of Friday's 12 paise slide to 94.93, so the currency has now given up ground in three sessions running.
Why the rupee is falling

Forex traders put the slide down to a stronger dollar, slight gains in U.S. Treasury yields and elevated crude oil prices, with geopolitical tension in West Asia weighing on sentiment. A recovery in the domestic markets cushioned the downside, which is why the rupee finished the day above its worst level rather than at it.
What a weaker rupee costs an importer

A weaker rupee makes every dollar-denominated purchase dearer, and the effect is immediate. Take a $10,000 import order. At Friday's rate of 94.93 it cost ₹9,49,300. At Monday's 95.22 the same order costs ₹9,52,200 — ₹2,900 more for a 29-paise move, and that is before customs duty, freight or insurance are added.

The rule of thumb is easier to remember than the arithmetic: every ₹1 the rupee falls adds ₹10,000 to a $10,000 bill. A shop that imports twice a year can absorb that. A trader placing monthly orders cannot, which is why the rate belongs in the price you quote, not in a footnote.
What it pays an exporter

The same move works in reverse for anyone who earns in dollars. A $10,000 export invoice that fetched ₹9,49,300 on Friday now brings in ₹9,52,200. An exporter whose costs are in rupees and whose price is in dollars therefore sees the margin widen as the rupee weakens, provided the rate has not already been locked with a forward contract.
What to do about it

For a small business the practical answer is to plan against a range rather than a single number. Check whether your margin still holds if the rupee moves another rupee in either direction, because a rate that flatters your numbers today can turn a profitable order into a break-even one next month. Re-run your landed cost with the current rate before you quote, and treat the exchange rate as one more line item that moves, the same way you treat freight or packaging.

None of this is a forecast. The rupee closed at 95.22 on October 26 after opening at 94.92, and where it goes next depends on crude prices, U.S. yields and events no calculator can see. What a calculator can do is tell you the number your margin can survive.
body_hinglish: Monday, October 26, 2026 ko rupee teesre din bhi gira aur dollar ke against 29 paise kam hokar 95.22 par band hua. Din ki shuruaat 94.92 par hui, din mein 95.26 tak gira aur 95.22 par band hua. Friday ko bhi 12 paise gir kar 94.93 par band hua tha, to teen session se rupee peeche ja raha hai.
Rupee kyun gir raha hai

Forex traders ke mutabik wajah hai mazboot dollar, US Treasury yields mein halki badhotri aur mehnga crude oil, aur West Asia ka geopolitical tension sentiment par bhaari pad raha hai. Domestic market mein recovery ne nuksan kam kiya, isliye rupee din ke sabse neeche level se upar band hua.
Kamzor rupee importer ko kitna mehnga padta hai

Kamzor rupee har dollar wali kharid ko mehnga kar deta hai, aur asar turant hota hai. Maan lo $10,000 ka import order hai. Friday ke 94.93 par iski cost ₹9,49,300 thi. Monday ke 95.22 par wahi order ₹9,52,200 padta hai — 29 paise ke move par ₹2,900 zyada, aur ye customs duty, freight ya insurance se pehle ki baat hai.

Yaad rakhne ka aasan rule: rupee jitna ₹1 girta hai, $10,000 ke bill par ₹10,000 jud jaata hai. Saal mein do baar import karne wala dukaan ise jhel lega. Har mahine order karne wala nahi, isliye rate ko apne quote ki price mein rakho, footnote mein nahi.
Exporter ko kitna milta hai

Jo dollar mein kamata hai, uske liye yahi move ulta kaam karta hai. Friday ko $10,000 ka export invoice ₹9,49,300 deta tha, ab ₹9,52,200 dega. Jis exporter ki cost rupee mein hai aur price dollar mein, uska margin rupee kamzor hone par badhta hai — bas rate forward contract se pehle se lock na ho.
Iska kya karna hai

Chhote business ke liye practical baat ye hai ki ek number ke bajaye ek range par plan karo. Dekho ki rupee ek rupaya idhar ya udhar move kare to bhi tumhara margin tikta hai ya nahi, kyunki aaj ka rate jo achha lag raha hai wo agle mahine order ko break-even bana sakta hai. Quote karne se pehle current rate par apna landed cost dobara chalao, aur exchange rate ko bhi ek aise line item ki tarah dekho jo move karta hai, jaise freight ya packaging.

Ye koi forecast nahi hai. October 26 ko rupee 94.92 par khula aur 95.22 par band hua, aur aage kya hoga wo crude prices, US yields aur un events par nirbhar karta hai jo koi calculator nahi dekh sakta. Calculator sirf itna bata sakta hai ki tumhara margin kaunsa number jhel sakta hai.

items.title: Govt to Bear Certification Costs for Small Exporters
items.dek: Micro and small exporters can claim up to 75% of certification costs under the Export Promotion Mission, with a ₹25 lakh yearly cap and EU CBAM cover.

cta.text: Certification is one more line in what a unit costs you. Put it beside packaging, freight and material and see the true per-unit cost before you quote a price.
cta.label: Open the Landed Cost Calculator

body_en: On October 23, 2026, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said the government is willing to bear the entire cost of "expensive" certification for micro and small enterprises that want to export, under the Export Promotion Mission. He asked both existing and new exporters to approach the Directorate General of Foreign Trade for the support.

The promise matters because certification is one of the first big bills a small exporter meets: the testing, inspection, conformity and traceability reports a buyer in Europe or the United States asks for before placing an order.
What the government announced

Goyal, speaking to reporters in Berlin, said: "Under the mission, we are willing to support everybody who wants to export anywhere in the world. We will give them support. For micro and small (enterprises), we are willing to literally take care of the entire cost of certification and others also, if there is some very expensive certification or process."

He added that the cost of complying with European Union regulations, including the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and the EU Deforestation Regulation, would be covered for micro and small enterprises. Support for bigger businesses would come on a graded basis. He also urged exporters across product categories and sectors to use the scheme, saying it would encourage new products, new markets and new exporters.
The mission and the money behind it

The Export Promotion Mission was approved in November 2025 with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for six financial years. It runs through two sub-schemes: Niryat Protsahan, with ₹10,401 crore, and Niryat Disha, with ₹14,659 crore.

The certification support sits inside a component called Trade Regulations, Accreditation and Compliance Enablement, or TRACE. It pays for the international testing, inspection, certification and other conformity work that opens a market. To use it, an exporter needs a valid Importer Exporter Code and a valid MSME Udyam registration number.

The published rates are tiered. For certifications on the notified Positive List, assistance is 60% of the actual cost net of taxes, or ₹25 lakh, whichever is lower. For the notified Priority Positive List, it is 75%, again capped at ₹25 lakh. The annual cap for one exporter under TRACE is ₹25 lakh.
The arithmetic of one certification claim

Suppose a laboratory test, a notified body and a traceability audit together cost ₹10,00,000 for your product line. On the Positive List, 60% of ₹10,00,000 is ₹6,00,000, because 10,00,000 × 60 ÷ 100 = 6,00,000. You pay the other ₹4,00,000.

If that same certification sits on the Priority Positive List, 75% of ₹10,00,000 is ₹7,50,000, so your own share falls to ₹2,50,000. The difference between the two lists is ₹1,50,000 on a bill of ₹10,00,000, which is worth checking before you file.

Now push the bill up. At ₹30,00,000 of certification cost, 75% works out to ₹22,50,000, still under the ceiling, so the cap does not bite. At ₹40,00,000, 75% would be ₹30,00,000, but the ceiling cuts the support to ₹25,00,000 and you carry the rest. The cap starts to matter once your certification bill crosses roughly ₹33,00,000, because 25,00,000 ÷ 75 × 100 is about ₹33,33,333.
Why the EU rules are the live part

The European Union is where the pressure is sharpest. India's exports to EU countries fell 4.57% to $72.4 billion in 2025-26 from $75.85 billion a year earlier, and the EU took about 17% of India's merchandise shipments. The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism asks exporters of steel, aluminium, cement and fertiliser to report the emissions locked into what they ship, and the EU Deforestation Regulation asks for proof that the product is not linked to deforested land.

Both need records a small factory often does not keep: energy bills, process data, supplier declarations. Meeting them means paying an auditor, a lab or a consultant, and that is exactly the bill TRACE is meant to share. The minister's remarks are significant because MSMEs had flagged the cost of reporting, certification, emissions monitoring and traceability as a burden that could make Indian goods costlier in Europe.
What it means for your shop or startup

If you already export, first check that your Udyam registration is current and your Importer Exporter Code is valid, because TRACE is closed without both. Then write down every certification, test report and audit your main buyer asks for, and price each one. That list is what you claim against, and it is also the number you have been absorbing quietly.

If you are exporting for the first time, work the cost into your unit price before you quote. Say the bill is ₹10,00,000 and you pay ₹2,50,000 of it yourself. Spread over 10,000 units that is ₹25 a unit, because 2,50,000 ÷ 10,000 = 25. Spread over 1,000 units it is ₹250 a unit. The grant is the same either way; the volume is what turns it into a margin.

One caution. This is a policy promise, and the detailed procedure, the notified positive and priority lists, and the claim window come from DGFT notifications. Read the notification before you spend, keep every invoice, and remember that assistance is paid on actual cost net of taxes. If you cannot find your certification on the notified list, ask DGFT before assuming it is covered.
body_hinglish: 23 October 2026 ko, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal ne kaha ki government Export Promotion Mission ke tehat micro aur small enterprises ke liye "expensive" certification ka poora kharcha uthane ko taiyar hai. Unhone purane aur naye dono exporters se kaha ki support ke liye Directorate General of Foreign Trade se sampark karein.

Ye vaada matter karta hai kyunki certification ek chhote exporter ka pehla bada bill hota hai: testing, inspection, conformity aur traceability reports, jo Europe ya United States ka buyer order dene se pehle maangta hai.
Government ne kya announce kiya

Berlin mein reporters se baat karte hue Goyal ne kaha: "Under the mission, we are willing to support everybody who wants to export anywhere in the world. We will give them support. For micro and small (enterprises), we are willing to literally take care of the entire cost of certification and others also, if there is some very expensive certification or process."

Unhone kaha ki European Union ke regulations, including Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism aur EU Deforestation Regulation, ka compliance kharcha micro aur small enterprises ke liye cover kiya jayega. Bade businesses ko graded basis par support milega. Unhone exporters se har product category aur sector mein scheme ka fayda uthane ko bhi kaha, aur kaha ki isse naye products, naye markets aur naye exporters badhenge.
Mission aur iske peeche ka paisa

Export Promotion Mission November 2025 mein approve hui thi, ₹25,060 crore ke outlay ke saath chhe financial years ke liye. Ye do sub-schemes se chalti hai: Niryat Protsahan, ₹10,401 crore ke saath, aur Niryat Disha, ₹14,659 crore ke saath.

Certification ka support ek component mein hai jiska naam Trade Regulations, Accreditation and Compliance Enablement, ya TRACE hai. Ye us international testing, inspection, certification aur conformity kaam ka paisa deta hai jo market kholta hai. Iske liye exporter ke paas valid Importer Exporter Code aur valid MSME Udyam registration number hona chahiye.

Published rates tiered hain. Notified Positive List ki certifications par assistance actual cost ka 60% hai, taxes ke baad, ya ₹25 lakh, jo kam ho. Notified Priority Positive List par ye 75% hai, phir bhi ₹25 lakh par capped. TRACE ke tehat ek exporter ke liye saalana cap ₹25 lakh hai.
Ek certification claim ka hisaab

Maano ek laboratory test, ek notified body aur ek traceability audit mil kar aapki product line ke liye ₹10,00,000 ka hote hain. Positive List par, ₹10,00,000 ka 60% ₹6,00,000 hai, kyunki 10,00,000 × 60 ÷ 100 = 6,00,000. Baaki ₹4,00,000 aap dete ho.

Agar wahi certification Priority Positive List par hai, to ₹10,00,000 ka 75% ₹7,50,000 hai, isliye aapka hissa ₹2,50,000 reh jaata hai. Dono lists ke beech ka farak ₹10,00,000 ke bill par ₹1,50,000 hai, isliye file karne se pehle ye check karna faayda deta hai.

Ab bill badhao. ₹30,00,000 ke certification cost par 75% matlab ₹22,50,000, jo ceiling se neeche hai, isliye cap nahi lagta. ₹40,00,000 par 75% ₹30,00,000 hota, lekin ceiling support ko ₹25,00,000 par kaat deti hai aur baaki aap uthate ho. Cap tab matter karta hai jab aapka certification bill lagbhag ₹33,00,000 se upar jaata hai, kyunki 25,00,000 ÷ 75 × 100 lagbhag ₹33,33,333 hai.
EU ke rules hi asli hissa kyun hain

European Union mein ye dabav sabse zyada hai. India ka EU countries ko export 4.57% giriya, 2025-26 mein $72.4 billion, jabki pichhle saal $75.85 billion tha, aur EU ne India ki merchandise shipments ka lagbhag 17% liya. Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism un exporters se, jo steel, aluminium, cement aur fertiliser bhejte hain, maangta hai ki wo apne shipment ki emissions report karein, aur EU Deforestation Regulation proof maangta hai ki product deforested zameen se juda nahi hai.

Dono ke liye wo records chahiye jo ek chhoti factory aksar nahi rakhti: energy bills, process data, supplier declarations. Inhe pura karne ka matlab hai auditor, lab ya consultant ka kharcha, aur yahi bill TRACE baantne ke liye bana hai. Minister ki baat isliye important hai kyunki MSMEs ne reporting, certification, emissions monitoring aur traceability ka kharcha ek bojh bataya tha jo Indian goods ko Europe mein mehnga kar sakta hai.
Aapki dukaan ya startup ke liye iska matlab

Agar aap pehle se export karte ho, to pehle ye dekho ki aapki Udyam registration current hai aur Importer Exporter Code valid hai, kyunki dono ke bina TRACE band hai. Phir har wo certification, test report aur audit likho jo aapka main buyer maangta hai, aur har ek ka price lagao. Wahi list aapke claim ka base hai, aur wahi number jo aap chupchap bhugat rahe the.

Agar aap pehli baar export kar rahe ho, to quote dene se pehle ye cost apne unit price mein daalo. Maano bill ₹10,00,000 ka hai aur aap usme se ₹2,50,000 dete ho. 10,000 units par ye ₹25 per unit hai, kyunki 2,50,000 ÷ 10,000 = 25. 1,000 units par ye ₹250 per unit hai. Grant dono mein same hai; volume hi ise margin banata hai.

Ek savdhani. Ye ek policy vaada hai, aur detailed procedure, notified positive aur priority lists, aur claim window DGFT notifications se aate hain. Kharch karne se pehle notification padho, har invoice sambhal kar rakho, aur yaad rakho ki assistance actual cost par milti hai, taxes ke baad. Agar aapki certification notified list par nahi milti, to ye maanne se pehle DGFT se poocho ki wo cover hai ya nahi.

items.title: GST Registration for Small E-Commerce Sellers Opens Nov 1
items.dek: Small sellers can register in a new state from November 1 using the platform's warehouse as their place of business, if monthly credit is under ₹2.5 lakh.

cta.text: Splitting a bill into base price and GST, or working back from a GST-inclusive price, is the same sum the new registration rule turns on.
cta.label: Open the GST Calculator

related.title: Marketplace Fees in India: A Seller's Guide

body_en: From November 1, 2026, a small seller who sells only through Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho or another e-commerce platform can register for GST in a new state without opening an office or a shop there. A senior finance ministry official said on October 22 that the system changes needed for the new route are ready and the facility will go live on the GST portal from the beginning of next month.

The route was proposed by the 57th GST Council earlier in October, under a new Rule 14B of the Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017. It is separate from the enforcement and refund changes the same Council approved. This one is about the paperwork that stops a seller from shipping to customers outside their home state.
What actually changes on November 1

Under the rules as they stand, a seller who wants to hold stock in another state and sell from there needs a GST registration in that state. That usually means a rented premises, an address proof and a separate compliance routine. Many small sellers stay in one state for exactly this reason.

Rule 14B offers an optional alternative. A small seller of goods who supplies exclusively through electronic commerce operators can declare the warehouse of the e-commerce platform as their principal place of business in that state. They do not need to set up their own office or shop there. The consent of the e-commerce operator is obtained through the system, so the platform has to agree before the registration goes through.

Prashanth Agarwal, a partner at PwC India, called it a radical reform that can have a positive impact beyond GST on the economy at large. He said e-commerce sellers are generally reluctant to expand beyond their home state because of the compliance requirement, and that letting platform players support these sellers through the GSTN platform should go a long way in solving that.
Who qualifies, and the ₹2.5 lakh rule

Three conditions decide whether this is for you. First, you must already have a physical presence and a GST registration in at least one state, and that state will remain your home state. Second, the registration obtained this way can be used only for supplies made through e-commerce platforms, not for your own counter sales in that state. Third, you must pass on input tax credit of not more than ₹2.5 lakh a month.
The third condition is the one to check with your accountant, because it is a ceiling on credit, not a ceiling on turnover.
The arithmetic of the ₹2.5 lakh ceiling

Input tax credit is the GST you have already paid on your purchases, which you set off against the GST you collect on your sales. At 18%, every ₹10,00,000 of purchases carries ₹1,80,000 of credit, because 10,00,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = 1,80,000. So a monthly credit ceiling of ₹2.5 lakh works out to roughly ₹13,00,000 to ₹14,00,000 of purchases a month at 18%.

Across a year, ₹2.5 lakh a month is ₹30,00,000 of credit. If your purchases run above that, this simplified route is not for you and you will keep registering the ordinary way. If you sell goods at 5% or 12%, the same ₹2.5 lakh of credit covers more purchases, because each rupee of purchase carries less tax.
What it costs you in extra filings

Every additional state registration means another GSTIN, and another monthly return. That is real work, and it is why a seller should add a state only when the sales there justify it. Say you sell ₹5,00,000 of goods in a month in one state and charge 18% GST. The tax inside that month's bills is ₹90,000, because 5,00,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = 90,000, and the customer pays ₹5,90,000 in all.

Now set that against the credit you would claim on the stock you moved into the state. If that stock cost ₹4,00,000, the credit on it is ₹72,000. The extra return you file each month is the price of holding stock locally and shipping in a day instead of a week.
What it means for your shop or startup

If you sell only through marketplaces and your monthly input tax credit stays under ₹2.5 lakh, this is the cheapest way to start selling in a second state. The first thing to check is whether your platform has opted into the consent process, because the registration cannot go through without it. Detailed circulars explaining the process and the related notifications are expected in the next few days, so read them before you apply rather than after.

Separately, notifications and circulars covering the refund changes approved by the Council are also expected soon, which matters if you sell zero-rated or exported goods. And the long-running dispute over Section 16(2)(c), which lets a genuine buyer lose credit when a supplier does not deposit tax, has gone to a committee of officers. Its report is expected within three months, it will then go to the Council, and any decision is targeted for implementation from April 1, 2027. That is the bigger number for most sellers, and it is still open.
body_hinglish: 1 November 2026 se, jo chhota seller sirf Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho ya kisi aur e-commerce platform par bechta hai, wo naye state mein GST registration karwa sakta hai bina wahan office ya dukaan khole. Ek senior finance ministry official ne 22 October ko kaha ki naye raaste ke liye zaroori system changes taiyar hain aur ye facility agle mahine ki shuruaat se GST portal par live ho jayegi.

Ye raasta 57th GST Council ne October ke shuru mein propose kiya tha, Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017 ke naye Rule 14B ke tehat. Ye usi Council ke enforcement aur refund wale changes se alag hai. Ye us paperwork ke baare mein hai jo seller ko apne home state ke bahar customers ko bhejne se rokta hai.
1 November se asli mein kya badalta hai

Abhi ke rules ke hisaab se, jo seller doosre state mein stock rakh kar wahan se bechna chahta hai, usse us state mein GST registration chahiye. Iska matlab aam taur par kiraye ka premises, address proof aur alag compliance routine. Bahut se chhote sellers sirf isi wajah se ek hi state mein rehte hain.

Rule 14B ek optional raasta deta hai. Jo chhota seller sirf electronic commerce operators ke through goods bechta hai, wo us state mein e-commerce platform ke warehouse ko apna principal place of business declare kar sakta hai. Unhe wahan apna office ya dukaan set up karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. E-commerce operator ki consent system ke through li jaati hai, isliye platform ko pehle haan kehna padta hai.

PwC India ke partner Prashanth Agarwal ne ise radical reform kaha jo GST se aage ja kar poori economy par positive asar daal sakta hai. Unhone kaha ki e-commerce sellers aam taur par compliance requirement ki wajah se apne home state se bahar jaane mein hichakte hain, aur platform players ko GSTN ke through in sellers ki madad karne dene se ye problem kaafi had tak hal ho sakti hai.
Kaun qualify karta hai, aur ₹2.5 lakh ka rule

Teen shartein tay karti hain ki ye aapke liye hai ya nahi. Pehli, aapke paas kam se kam ek state mein physical presence aur GST registration pehle se hona chahiye, aur wahi state aapka home state rahega. Doosri, is tarah liya gaya registration sirf e-commerce platforms ke through ki gayi supplies ke liye use ho sakta hai, us state mein aapki apni counter sales ke liye nahi. Teesri, aapko mahine mein ₹2.5 lakh se zyada input tax credit pass on nahi karna chahiye.
Teesri shart apne accountant se check karein, kyunki ye credit par limit hai, turnover par nahi.
₹2.5 lakh ceiling ka hisaab

Input tax credit wo GST hai jo aap apni kharidari par pehle hi de chuke ho, aur jise aap apni sales par collect kiye gaye GST se set off karte ho. 18% par, har ₹10,00,000 ki kharidari par ₹1,80,000 ka credit banta hai, kyunki 10,00,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = 1,80,000. Isliye ₹2.5 lakh ki monthly credit limit 18% par lagbhag ₹13,00,000 se ₹14,00,000 ki mahine ki kharidari ke barabar hai.

Saal bhar mein ₹2.5 lakh mahina matlab ₹30,00,000 ka credit. Agar aapki kharidari isse zyada hai, to ye simplified raasta aapke liye nahi hai aur aap purane tareeke se hi registration karte rahenge. Agar aap 5% ya 12% ke goods bechte ho, to wahi ₹2.5 lakh ka credit zyada kharidari cover karta hai, kyunki har rupaye ki kharidari par kam tax hota hai.
Extra filings ka kitna kharcha

Har extra state registration ka matlab ek aur GSTIN, aur ek aur monthly return. Ye asli kaam hai, isliye seller ko state tabhi add karna chahiye jab wahan ki sales ise justify karein. Maano aap ek state mein ek mahine mein ₹5,00,000 ke goods bechte ho aur 18% GST lagate ho. Us mahine ke bills mein tax ₹90,000 hai, kyunki 5,00,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = 90,000, aur customer kul ₹5,90,000 deta hai.

Ab ise us credit se compare karo jo us state mein bheje gaye stock par milega. Agar wo stock ₹4,00,000 ka tha, to uspar credit ₹72,000 hai. Har mahine ki ye extra return us price ka hissa hai jo aap local stock rakhne aur hafte ki jagah ek din mein ship karne ke liye dete ho.
Aapki dukaan ya startup ke liye iska matlab

Agar aap sirf marketplaces par bechte ho aur aapka monthly input tax credit ₹2.5 lakh se neeche rehta hai, to doosre state mein bechna shuru karne ka ye sabse sasta raasta hai. Sabse pehle ye dekho ki aapka platform consent process mein shamil hua hai ya nahi, kyunki iske bina registration nahi ho sakta. Process samjhane wale detailed circulars aur related notifications agle kuch dinon mein aane ki umeed hai, isliye apply karne se pehle padho, baad mein nahi.

Alag se, Council ne jo refund changes approve kiye hain, unke notifications aur circulars bhi jaldi aane ki umeed hai, jo aapke liye matter karta hai agar aap zero-rated ya export goods bechte ho. Aur Section 16(2)(c) ka purana vivaad, jisme supplier tax jama na kare to ek genuine buyer ka credit chala jaata hai, officers ki committee ko bhej diya gaya hai. Uski report teen mahine mein aane ki umeed hai, phir ye Council ke saamne jaayegi, aur koi bhi faisla 1 April 2027 se lagu karne ka target hai. Zyadatar sellers ke liye yahi bada number hai, aur ye abhi khula hai.

items.title: RBI Hiked the Repo Rate to 5.50%: What It Costs Your Loan
items.dek: RBI's October minutes show a unanimous 25 bps hike to 5.50% and a shift to calibrated tightening. Here is what two more hikes do to a small business loan.

cta.text: Put your loan amount, rate and tenure in and see what a higher rate does to your monthly EMI.
cta.label: Open the Loan EMI Calculator

body_en: The Reserve Bank of India released the minutes of its 63rd Monetary Policy Committee meeting on October 21, 2026. The committee, chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% at its October 5 to 7 meeting, and changed its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening.
What the minutes say the RBI decided

The repo rate is now 5.50%, up from 5.25%. The standing deposit facility rate moved to 5.25%, and the marginal standing facility rate and the Bank Rate moved to 5.75%. The rate rise itself was unanimous. The change of stance was not. Two external members, Dr. Nagesh Kumar and Professor Ram Singh, wanted to keep the neutral stance, arguing that a tightening signal can read as the start of a long cycle of rate increases.
Why the committee is worried about prices

Consumer price inflation rose to 4.8% in August 2026 from 4.5% in July. Food and fuel led the increase, but core inflation, which strips out food and fuel, also rose, to 4.2%. The RBI expects CPI inflation to average close to 5.8% over the next three quarters, and projects it at 6.0% in the December quarter and 5.7% in the March quarter. The target is 4%. On growth, the RBI kept its projection for the year at 7.1%.
The arithmetic of a 25 basis point hike

One basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point, so 25 basis points is 0.25%. On a loan of ₹10,00,000, an extra 0.25% is ₹2,500 of interest a year, because 10,00,000 × 0.25 ÷ 100 = 2,500. Stretch that over five years and the same loan costs ₹12,500 more. On a ₹50,00,000 loan the same 0.25% is ₹12,500 a year. Two further hikes of 25 basis points each would add 0.50% in total, which is ₹5,000 a year, or ₹25,000 across five years, on ₹10,00,000.
Why 0.25% is not a rounding error

For a business, ₹5,000 a year is often the whole annual profit on a small order book. If a shop earns a 10% margin, it has to sell ₹50,000 of extra stock to recover that ₹5,000, because 5,000 ÷ 10% = 50,000. On a working capital line of ₹20,00,000, two hikes add ₹10,000 a year of interest. That money leaves the business before the owner's salary, so it lands straight on the monthly budget.
What it means for your shop or startup

If you have a floating-rate business loan or an overdraft, the next EMI or interest debit will be higher. Check the reset date on the sanction letter, because many business loans reprice every quarter while some retail loans reprice only once a year. If you are about to borrow, ask for the total interest over the full tenure, not just the EMI, since a longer tenure hides a bigger interest bill. If you hold a fixed deposit or a recurring deposit, the same cycle usually works in your favour over time, because new deposits get the higher rate. And if you are planning a big purchase on credit, run the numbers at a rate 0.50% higher than today's quote, so the next hike does not surprise you.
body_hinglish: Reserve Bank of India ne 21 October 2026 ko apni 63rd Monetary Policy Committee meeting ke minutes jaari kiye. Governor Sanjay Malhotra ki adhyakshta wali committee ne 5 se 7 October ki meeting mein repo rate 25 basis points badha kar 5.50% karne ka unanimous faisla kiya, aur apna stance neutral se calibrated tightening kar diya.
Minutes ke mutabik RBI ne kya kiya

Repo rate ab 5.50% hai, jo pehle 5.25% tha. Standing deposit facility rate 5.25% ho gaya, aur marginal standing facility rate aur Bank Rate 5.75% ho gaye. Rate badhane ka faisla sabhi members ne ek saath liya. Lekin stance badalne par sabhi sehmat nahi the. Do external members, Dr. Nagesh Kumar aur Professor Ram Singh, neutral stance banaye rakhna chahte the. Unka kehna tha ki tightening ka signal logon ko ek lambi rate-hike cycle ka ishara de sakta hai.
Committee ko mehngai ki chinta kyun hai

August 2026 mein consumer price inflation July ke 4.5% se badh kar 4.8% ho gayi. Khane aur fuel ki keematein iski main wajah thi, lekin core inflation, jisme khana aur fuel nahi ginte, woh bhi badh kar 4.2% ho gayi. RBI ko ummeed hai ki agle teen quarters mein CPI inflation lagbhag 5.8% rahegi. Uska anumaan hai ki December quarter mein 6.0% aur March quarter mein 5.7% rahegi. Target 4% hai. Growth par, RBI ne is saal ke liye apna anumaan 7.1% hi rakha.
25 basis point hike ka hisaab

Ek basis point ek percentage point ka sauwan hissa hota hai, isliye 25 basis points matlab 0.25%. ₹10,00,000 ke loan par extra 0.25% saal ka ₹2,500 interest banata hai, kyunki 10,00,000 × 0.25 ÷ 100 = 2,500. Isi loan par paanch saal mein yeh ₹12,500 zyada ho jata hai. ₹50,00,000 ke loan par wahi 0.25% saal ka ₹12,500 hai. Agar 25-25 basis points ke do aur hike aate hain, to total 0.50% badhega: ₹10,00,000 par saal ka ₹5,000, ya paanch saal mein ₹25,000.
0.25% koi chhoti baat nahi hai

Ek business ke liye saal ka ₹5,000 aksar poore chhote order book ka profit hota hai. Agar dukaan ka margin 10% hai, to yeh ₹5,000 wapas kamane ke liye usse ₹50,000 ka extra maal bechna padega, kyunki 5,000 ÷ 10% = 50,000. ₹20,00,000 ke working capital loan par do hikes saal ka ₹10,000 interest jodte hain. Yeh paisa owner ki salary se pehle cash flow se nikalta hai, isliye seedha monthly budget par asar karta hai.
Aapki dukaan ya startup ke liye iska matlab

Agar aapke paas floating-rate business loan ya overdraft hai, to agla EMI ya interest debit zyada hoga. Sanction letter par reset date zaroor dekhein, kyunki kai business loans har quarter reprice hote hain, jabki kuch retail loans saal mein ek baar. Agar aap naya loan lene wale hain, to sirf EMI nahi, poore tenure ka total interest poochhein, kyunki lambi tenure bada interest bill chhupa deti hai. Agar aapke paas fixed deposit ya recurring deposit hai, to aam taur par yeh cycle samay ke saath aapke faayde mein kaam karta hai, kyunki naye deposits ko zyada rate milta hai. Aur agar aap credit par koi badi kharidari plan kar rahe hain, to aaj ke quote se 0.50% zyada rate par hisaab lagayein, taaki agla hike aapko chaunkay na.

items.title: Amazon Festive Sale Lifted Seller Sales 3.5x in Week One
items.dek: Amazon's festive sale lifted seller sales 3.5x in week one, and zero referral fees below ₹1,000 did part of it. Here is what that means for your price.

cta.text: Put your own price, commission and shipping in and see what you actually keep.
cta.label: Open the Marketplace Fee Calculator

body_en: Amazon India's Great Indian Festival 2026 opened with seller sales running 3.5 times normal levels in its first week, and products selling more than twice as fast, according to ET Retail. Seller participation rose nearly 30% year on year to a record high, and more than 70% of the participating small and medium businesses came from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
A festival week is a strange thing to measure. The number is real, but it is measured against an ordinary week, not against last October. Read it as a spike, not as a new normal.
What the numbers actually say

The count of SMBs crossing ₹10 lakh in sales grew more than 4.6 times in that first week, and the number of sellers crossing ₹1 crore grew over 1.5 times. Among sellers who were new to the platform, units sold rose more than 2.5 times, the count crossing ₹1 lakh grew 2.4 times, and those crossing ₹10 lakh increased more than fourfold.

Women entrepreneurs in Amazon Saheli recorded sales spikes of up to 10 times, and sellers in Amazon Karigar, the artisans programme, grew more than 1.5 times. The top five categories by seller sales were jewellery, shoes, automotive, major appliances and wireless products.
Why the ₹10 lakh line is the one to watch

Growth multiples flatter small bases. A seller who did ₹1 lakh in a normal week and ₹10 lakh in the festival week has grown ten times, and that is a genuine achievement — but it also means the next ordinary week will look like a collapse. If you hired staff or bought stock on the strength of a festival week, the arithmetic of the week after is what pays for it.

Compare the two groups. The number of sellers crossing ₹1 crore grew 1.5 times, while those crossing ₹10 lakh grew 4.6 times. The bigger the base, the harder the multiple. That is normal, and it is why a headline multiple should never be read as a promise of scale.
The fee change doing part of the work

Amazon attributed part of the momentum to changes in its seller fee structure, including zero referral fees on products priced below ₹1,000. In the first 24 hours of the festival, the number of sellers offering products below ₹500 who recorded a tenfold sales spike grew more than two times compared with a year earlier.

Here is the arithmetic of why that threshold matters. Suppose your referral fee is 20% and you sell at ₹1,000. The fee is ₹200, so you keep ₹800 before shipping and any closing fee. Sell the same item at ₹900 with no referral fee and you keep ₹900. You take ₹100 less from the customer and still keep ₹100 more. That is the whole argument for knowing where your price sits relative to the threshold.
What this means if you sell online
Check where your price sits. If your best-selling item is priced just above a fee threshold, the arithmetic above applies to every single order. Move the price deliberately, not by accident.
Do not build fixed costs on a spike. A 3.5 times week is a week. Warehouse rent, extra staff and a large inventory bet are monthly costs, and they do not shrink when the traffic goes back to normal.

Read your payout ratio, not your sales figure. The dashboard shows what the customer paid. Your bank account shows what you kept. Those are different numbers, and the gap is fees, shipping and returns.

Plan the next sale now. Amazon ran a seller acquisition campaign across more than 150 cities and towns and a Festive Readiness Seller Academy with ten sessions. The sellers who crossed ₹10 lakh in week one had listings, stock and ad budgets ready before the sale opened, not during it.
Do this before the next festival

Take your five best-selling items and write down the price, the commission percentage, the shipping you pay and the returns you expect. Work out what you actually keep on each one. Most sellers find one or two items earn far less than the sales report suggests, and a small price correction before the next sale is worth more than any discount you can offer during it.
body_hinglish: Amazon India ke Great Indian Festival 2026 ke pehle hafte mein seller sales normal level se 3.5 guna rahi, aur products do guna se zyada tezi se bike, ET Retail ke mutabik. Seller participation pichhle saal se takriban 30% badhi aur record par pahunchi, aur participate karne wale small aur medium businesses mein se 70% se zyada Tier 2 aur Tier 3 shehron se the.
Festival ka hafta naapna ajeeb hota hai. Number sach hai, par woh ek aam hafte se compare kiya gaya hai, pichhle October se nahi. Ise spike samjho, naya normal nahi.
Numbers asal mein kya kehte hain

Jo SMBs ₹10 lakh ke sales cross kare, unki ginti us pehle hafte mein 4.6 guna se zyada badhi, aur ₹1 crore cross karne wale sellers 1.5 guna se zyada badhe. Naye sellers mein units sold 2.5 guna se zyada badhe, ₹1 lakh cross karne wale 2.4 guna badhe, aur ₹10 lakh cross karne wale chaar guna se zyada.

Amazon Saheli ki women entrepreneurs ne 10 guna tak ke sales spike dekhe, aur Amazon Karigar ke artisans 1.5 guna se zyada badhe. Seller sales ke hisaab se top paanch categories jewellery, shoes, automotive, major appliances aur wireless products thi.
₹10 lakh ki line par nazar kyun rakhni chahiye

Growth multiples chhote base ko hawa deti hain. Jo seller aam hafte mein ₹1 lakh karta tha aur festival hafte mein ₹10 lakh, usne das guna growth ki, aur ye asli achievement hai — par iska matlab ye bhi hai ki agla aam hafta collapse jaisa lagega. Agar aapne festival hafte ke bharose staff rakha ya stock kharida, to us agle hafte ka hisaab hi iska paisa deta hai.

Do groups ko compare karo. ₹1 crore cross karne wale sellers 1.5 guna badhe, aur ₹10 lakh cross karne wale 4.6 guna. Base jitna bada, multiple utna mushkil. Ye normal hai, aur isliye headline multiple ko kabhi scale ka wada nahi samajhna chahiye.
Fees mein badlav jo kaam kar raha hai

Amazon ne momentum ka ek hissa apne seller fee structure ke badlav ko diya, jisme ₹1,000 se kam ke products par zero referral fees shamil hai. Festival ke pehle 24 ghanton mein, ₹500 se kam ke products bechne wale sellers jinhone das guna sales spike dekha, unki ginti pichhle saal se do guna se zyada badhi.

Ye threshold kyun maayne rakhta hai, uska arithmetic dekho. Maan lo referral fee 20% hai aur aap ₹1,000 par bechte ho. Fee ₹200 hai, to shipping aur closing fee se pehle aap ₹800 rakhte ho. Wahi item ₹900 par bina referral fee becho to ₹900 rakhte ho. Customer se ₹100 kam lete ho aur phir bhi ₹100 zyada rakhte ho. Threshold ke hisaab se aapka price kahan hai, ye jaanna poori baat hai.
Agar aap online bechte ho to iska matlab
Dekho aapka price kahan baithta hai. Agar aapka best-selling item kisi fee threshold se bas thoda upar hai, to upar ka arithmetic har order par lagta hai. Price deliberately badlo, galti se nahi.
Spike par fixed cost mat banao. 3.5 guna hafta ek hafta hai. Warehouse rent, extra staff aur bada inventory bet mahine ka kharcha hain, aur traffic normal hone par woh kam nahi hote.

Apna payout ratio padho, sales figure nahi. Dashboard dikhata hai customer ne kitna diya. Bank account dikhata hai aapne kitna rakha. Ye do alag numbers hain, aur beech ka gap fees, shipping aur returns hai.

Agli sale ki planning ab karo. Amazon ne 150 se zyada shehron aur towns mein seller acquisition campaign chalaya aur das sessions ki Festive Readiness Seller Academy chalayi. Jo sellers pehle hafte mein ₹10 lakh cross kare, unke listings, stock aur ad budget sale khulne se pehle ready the, sale ke dauraan nahi.
Agle festival se pehle ye karo

Apne paanch best-selling items lo aur price, commission percentage, jo shipping aap dete ho aur jo returns expect karte ho, sab likho. Har item par aap asal mein kitna rakhte ho, nikaalo. Zyadatar sellers paate hain ki ek-do items sales report se kaafi kam kama rahe hain, aur agli sale se pehle chhota price correction us sale ke dauraan diye gaye kisi bhi discount se zyada kaam ka hai.

items.title: UPI MDR Is Deferred to After Diwali: What a Shop Will Actually Pay
items.dek: NPCI has pushed the 0.4% merchant fee on UPI payments above ₹2,000 to after Diwali. Here is the arithmetic of what that fee costs a small shop, and who is spared.

cta.text: A per-sale fee is a variable cost. See what it does to what each sale contributes.
cta.label: Open the Contribution Margin Calculator

body_en: India's biggest change to digital payments in years has been put on hold. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has deferred the merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions until after Diwali, just two days before it was due to start on October 15. The fee structure itself is unchanged — only the date moved.

For anyone who takes UPI at a counter, that means a few more weeks of free collections. It is a delay, not a cancellation. Here is what the rule says, what the fee costs in rupees, and what a shop should do before the new date arrives.
What NPCI actually announced

NPCI said the UPI and Services Steering Committee decided to implement MDR on select person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions "immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately." A source confirmed to Business Standard that there will be no change in the MDR structure. Only the start date has been pushed back.

An MDR is a fee a merchant pays to the bank and the payment company that process a digital transaction. Until now, UPI merchant payments carried no such fee for the merchant. That is what is about to change.
What 0.4% means in rupees
The levy is set at 0.40% on UPI payments to merchants above ₹2,000, and it is capped at ₹300. Some categories, including bill payments, fuel and education, attract a flat ₹5 instead.

Percentage fees feel tiny until you put them next to real sales. A ₹5,000 payment costs 0.40% of ₹5,000, which is ₹20. A ₹10,000 payment costs ₹40. A shop that collects ₹1,00,000 a month in merchant UPI payments pays about ₹400 a month, or roughly ₹4,800 over a year.

Now compare that with profit, not turnover. If the same shop runs at a 5% net margin, ₹1,00,000 of sales leaves ₹5,000 of profit. A ₹400 fee is 8% of that profit gone. On a thin margin, a fee that looks like a rounding error on the bill is a real slice of what the owner keeps.
Who pays, and who does not

The charge is aimed at merchant payments, not person-to-person transfers. It applies only to UPI payments above ₹2,000, so small everyday payments stay outside the levy. The flat ₹5 applies to a short list of categories rather than everything.
The cap matters for large bills. A ₹75,000 payment at 0.40% would work out to ₹300, so the cap bites at that level — anything bigger still costs ₹300, not more.

Business Standard reported that UPI recorded a record average of 802 million transactions a day in September, with an average daily value of ₹97,913 crore. A fee of 0.40% on that volume is a large amount of money changing hands across the system — which is why traders fought it and why the delay happened.
Why the delay happened

Timing. The fee was due to start on October 15, in the middle of the festive season, when retail volumes peak. Deferring it gives merchants a breather through their busiest weeks, while keeping the rule itself on the books.
It is worth reading the delay for what it is: a pause for the calendar, not a reversal of policy. Planning for the fee to arrive after Diwali is the safer assumption.
What a shop owner should do before the new date

First, work out the number for your own counter. Take your monthly merchant UPI collections above ₹2,000, multiply by 0.40%, and apply the ₹300 cap to any single large payment. That figure is the extra cost you are about to carry.

Second, treat it as a variable cost, because that is what it is. It rises with every sale, exactly like packaging or shipping. Add it to your cost per sale and watch what is left to cover rent, salaries and your own take-home.

Third, do not panic-price. A ₹20 cost on a ₹5,000 sale does not justify a price rise on its own. Decide on pricing with the full margin in view, and only for the categories where the fee actually bites.
And keep accepting UPI. The fee is small, the volumes are large, and customers have made their choice. The right response is to know the cost to the rupee, not to turn customers away at the counter.
body_hinglish: Digital payments ka sabse bada badlav kuch waqt ke liye ruk gaya hai. National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) ne select UPI transactions par merchant discount rate (MDR) ko Diwali ke baad tak tal diya hai — shuru hone se sirf do din pehle, jab woh 15 October ko lagu hona tha. Fee structure mein koi badlav nahi hua, sirf tareekh aage khiski hai.

Counter par UPI lene wale ke liye iska matlab hai kuch hafte aur free collection. Ye rok hai, rad nahi. Aage samjhiye ki rule kya kehta hai, rupaye mein kitna padta hai, aur nayi tareekh se pehle dukaan ko kya karna chahiye.
NPCI ne asal mein kya kaha

NPCI ne kaha ki UPI and Services Steering Committee ne decide kiya hai ki select person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions par MDR "immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately" lagu hoga. Business Standard ko ek source ne bataya ki MDR structure mein koi badlav nahi hoga. Sirf shuru hone ki tareekh aage badhi hai.

MDR woh fee hai jo merchant bank aur payment company ko deta hai, jo digital transaction process karti hai. Ab tak UPI merchant payments par merchant ko aisi koi fee nahi padti thi. Yahi badalne wala hai.
0.4% ka matlab rupaye mein
Levy ₹2,000 se upar wale UPI merchant payments par 0.40% hai, aur iski cap ₹300 hai. Kuch categories, jaise bill payments, fuel aur education, par flat ₹5 lagta hai.

Percentage fee chhoti lagti hai jab tak aap usse asli sales ke saath na rakhein. ₹5,000 ke payment par 0.40% matlab ₹20. ₹10,000 ke payment par ₹40. Jo dukaan mahine mein ₹1,00,000 merchant UPI collect karti hai, woh mahine ke lagbhag ₹400 deti hai, ya saal ke karib ₹4,800.

Ab isse turnover ke saath nahi, profit ke saath compare kariye. Agar wahi dukaan 5% net margin par chalti hai, to ₹1,00,000 ki sales se ₹5,000 profit bachta hai. ₹400 ki fee us profit ka 8% hai. Patle margin par, jo fee bill par rounding error lagti hai, woh owner ki kamai ka asli hissa hai.
Kaun deta hai, kaun nahi

Ye charge merchant payments ke liye hai, person-to-person transfers ke liye nahi. Ye sirf ₹2,000 se upar wale UPI payments par lagta hai, isliye chhote rozana payments is levy se bahar rehte hain. Flat ₹5 thodi si categories par lagta hai, sab par nahi.
Cap bade bills ke liye maayne rakhta hai. ₹75,000 ke payment par 0.40% matlab ₹300, isliye cap wahi se lagu hoti hai — usse bada koi bhi payment bhi ₹300 hi hota hai, zyada nahi.

Business Standard ne bataya ki September mein UPI ne ek din mein record average 802 million transactions kiye, aur average daily value ₹97,913 crore rahi. Us volume par 0.40% fee ka matlab hai poore system mein badi rakam ka lena-dena — isi liye traders ne virodh kiya aur isi liye ye delay hua.
Delay kyun hua

Timing. Fee 15 October se shuru honi thi, festive season ke beech, jab retail volumes sabse zyada hote hain. Isse talne se merchants ko unke sabse busy hafton mein rahat mili, lekin rule khud kitab mein bana hua hai.
Is delay ko waise padhiye jaise woh hai: calendar ke liye ruk, policy ka palat nahi. Ye maan kar chaliye ki fee Diwali ke baad aa jaayegi — yahi safe assumption hai.
Nayi tareekh se pehle dukaan ko kya karna chahiye

Pehle apne counter ka number nikaliye. Apni monthly merchant UPI collections jo ₹2,000 se upar hain, unhe 0.40% se multiply kariye, aur kisi ek bade payment par ₹300 ki cap lagaiye. Wahi figure aapki aane wali extra cost hai.

Doosre, ise variable cost maaniye, kyunki woh hai. Ye har sale ke saath badhti hai, bilkul packaging ya shipping ki tarah. Ise apni cost per sale mein jodiye aur dekhiye ki rent, salary aur apni kamai ke liye kitna bachta hai.

Teesre, ghabra kar price na badhaiye. ₹5,000 ki sale par ₹20 ki cost apne aap mein price badhane ka reason nahi hai. Pricing poore margin ko dekh kar tay kariye, aur sirf un categories mein jahan fee asli mein lagti hai.
Aur UPI lena jaari rakhiye. Fee chhoti hai, volumes bade hain, aur customers apna faisla kar chuke hain. Sahi jawab ye hai ki cost ko rupaye tak jaaniye, counter par customer ko lautane ka nahi.

items.title: Polygons Spoons Net Worth After Shark Tank USA Deal
